title: Days of the Week and the Calendar
subject: math

sections.body: There are 7 days in a week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. After Sunday, the week starts again with Monday. (In some countries a week starts on Sunday. Both ways have 7 days.)
A calendar shows the days in rows of 7. Each row is one week. A year has 12 months. Move down one row and you move 7 days on, to the same day of the week.
To count on, say the days in order. If today is Friday, then in 2 days it is Sunday: Saturday is 1, Sunday is 2. Two weeks is 7 + 7 = 14 days.
Look at a real calendar. Put your finger on today. Move down one row. What day is it? How many days did you move?
Use your own calendar at home: mark one family event and count the days until it, first in ones, then in weeks. Later lessons show that the calendar repeats every 7 days.

hints: Say the days in order. What happens after the last day of the week?
The week starts again from the beginning.
Example: the day after Saturday is Sunday. Use the same steps, but remember the week starts again after its last day.
quiz.explain: After Sunday the week starts again, so the next day is Monday.

quiz.q: Today is Monday. What day will it be in 3 days?
hints: Count on from today. Do not count today itself.
Say 'Tuesday is 1', then keep counting up to 3.
Example: from Saturday, 2 days on is Monday (Sunday is 1, Monday is 2). Count 3 days on from Monday.
quiz.explain: Tuesday is 1, Wednesday is 2, Thursday is 3. It will be Thursday.

quiz.q: How many days are in 2 weeks?
hints: How many days are in one week?
Two weeks is two groups of 7.
Example: 3 weeks is 7 + 7 + 7 = 21 days. Now do it for 2 weeks.
